questions.question: Shipping papers:

options.text: Are not required for most shipments.
Must be stored in a special compartment in the cab.
Can be kept as a digital file.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments. They tell drivers and dock workers about the dangers of the cargo.

questions.question: When accepting hazardous materials, a driver should check that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping papers to the markings and labels on the packages when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials laws are controlled by:
questions.explanation: Because hazardous materials are dangerous, federal, state, and local governments all have regulations for transporting them.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue while driving, you should take a break:
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least every two hours or after every 100 miles of driving to prevent fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: Stopping distance is mainly affected by:
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver, you should:
questions.explanation: Give distracted drivers plenty of room. Be careful when passing because they may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: To accept a package of hazardous materials, a driver needs:
questions.explanation: If a package is not clearly unsafe and follows the Hazardous Materials Regulations, you can accept the shipper's certification that it is properly packaged.

questions.question: When inspecting the engine, you should not:

options.text: Check the coolant level in the radiator.
Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.explanation: During engine inspections, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid. Do not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads. Be extra careful crossing bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts indicates they may be loose. Check and tighten the nuts if you see rust.

questions.question: When you pull over on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Which action does NOT reduce driving distractions?
questions.explanation: To avoid distractions, pre-program your radio, plan your route ahead of time, and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: During an inspection, your brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: Check for cracked drums and brake pads or shoes that have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them. Pads and shoes must be clean and not worn too thin.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach a 0.02 percent blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects driving ability before reaching the legal limit. A 200-pound person reaches a BAC of 0.02 percent after just one drink.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy or electronic image of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the initial carrier accepts the materials. For hazardous waste, keep records for three years.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be transported in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Heaters are not allowed when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: What should you do with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Put them on the front of the vehicle.
Put them on the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels and rims are not safe. Replace any damaged wheels and rims.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, you should not use:
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers or packaging when loading or unloading hazardous materials.

questions.question: On an uphill grade, gravity will:

options.text: Make your vehicle swerve to the left.

questions.explanation: When driving uphill, gravity pulls your vehicle backward and slows it down.

questions.question: On a steep downhill, what should be your main way to slow down?
questions.explanation: Use your engine to slow down on steep hills. Downshift and reduce speed before going downhill.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is allowed?
questions.explanation: Steering wheel play should not exceed 10 degrees. More than this makes the vehicle hard to steer.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does no spray from other vehicles mean?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught on the underside of the vehicle.
The tires have soaked up all the moisture.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road is wet but other vehicles are not spraying water, ice has formed on the road. Drive carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are driving slower than traffic, stay in the right lane if possible. This lets faster traffic pass safely.

questions.question: Can retreaded tires be used on a school bus?

options.text: No, they cannot be used on a school bus.

questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They may only be used on the rear axles.

questions.question: Where should the identification number for hazardous material appear?

options.text: On a bumper sticker on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the packaging and shipping papers. It must also appear on cargo tanks and bulk packaging.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration good for your vehicle?

options.text: No, it can damage the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: You must check tire pressure before each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check pressure.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of a trailer load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Is it important to keep space between your vehicle and other vehicles?

options.text: It is a waste of time.

questions.explanation: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is essential for safety. This gives you room to stop safely without hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: What should a pre-trip inspection include?

options.text: Spraying WD-40 into the air filter.

questions.explanation: A pre-trip inspection includes checking engine compartment components, including the engine oil level.
